contribution.role: External contributor proposing a generic sidebar extension API and separately maintaining the Sidebar Steroids add-on
contribution.scope: Plan one generic, backward-compatible sidebar extension seam in upstream Gentle Shell; keep Sidebar Steroids product behavior in a separate Pi package and keep attribution documentation local unless upstream maintainers request it.
contribution.historyAttributionPolicy: Attribute only file-level changes with an explicit diff against the pinned upstream base. The three local commits beyond the pinned base are not attributed to Sidebar Steroids.

delivery.installationMechanism: Install as a Pi package through Pi's package manager; do not patch or overwrite an installed gentle-pi or gentle-shell.
delivery.compatibilityStrategy: Discover the optional upstream sidebar extension API by capability. If it is absent or incompatible, fail closed with a clear compatibility message and leave the existing Status sidebar unchanged. Do not monkey-patch the upstream package.
delivery.packageIdentityNote: The provisional package name is subject to package-registry availability and trademark review; it must not be presented as official upstream branding.
delivery.sourceRepositoryStrategy: Maintain the installable Sidebar Steroids product in a dedicated repository with a distinct primary identity, provisionally andrikonbeat/sidebar-steroids.
delivery.currentRepositoryRole: Use this checkout as the upstream reference and preparation surface for a generic, independently reviewable sidebar host API contribution. Do not mix product-specific behavior into that upstream candidate.
delivery.remoteRepositoryAction: Repository creation, npm publication, pull requests, and releases remain separate human-owned actions.

plannedUpstreamChanges.purpose: Define a small, versioned public contract for optional third-party sidebar extensions without importing add-on-specific Git, Files, or Sidebar Steroids behavior.
plannedUpstreamChanges.publicContractImpact: Additive and opt-in. Existing sidebar behavior and defaults remain unchanged when no extension registers.
plannedUpstreamChanges.attributionMarkerStrategy: Use one sidebar-extension-api marker at the public registration seam; do not mark individual contract lines.

plannedUpstreamChanges.purpose: Expose the existing terminal-owned sidebar registration boundary through the generic extension contract.
plannedUpstreamChanges.publicContractImpact: Additive API surface only; current internal callers and Status rendering remain compatible.
plannedUpstreamChanges.attributionMarkerStrategy: Use one sidebar-extension-api marker immediately around the adapter or registration seam.

plannedUpstreamChanges.purpose: Allow an opted-in extension to participate in the fullscreen rail lifecycle and disposal without embedding product-specific rendering logic.
plannedUpstreamChanges.publicContractImpact: No default visual change. Lifecycle and rendering behavior change only for a registered compatible extension.
plannedUpstreamChanges.attributionMarkerStrategy: Use one sidebar-extension-api marker at the render and disposal bridge seam.

plannedUpstreamChanges.purpose: Wire the upstream extension entry point to the public sidebar extension contract during host initialization.
plannedUpstreamChanges.publicContractImpact: Host initialization exposes the opt-in seam without changing the default Status view.
plannedUpstreamChanges.attributionMarkerStrategy: Use one sidebar-extension-api marker at the initialization call seam.

plannedUpstreamChanges.purpose: Test the generic contract's registration, compatibility, and disposal semantics independently of any product add-on.
plannedUpstreamChanges.publicContractImpact: No runtime contract change; tests define the proposed backward-compatible behavior.
plannedUpstreamChanges.attributionMarkerStrategy: No source marker: test attribution is carried by Git history and this manifest.

plannedUpstreamChanges.purpose: Verify that extension registration is opt-in, leaves the default Status sidebar unchanged, and cleans up safely.
plannedUpstreamChanges.publicContractImpact: No runtime contract change; tests protect the existing default behavior.
plannedUpstreamChanges.attributionMarkerStrategy: No source marker: test attribution is carried by Git history and this manifest.

plannedUpstreamChanges.purpose: Document the generic extension lifecycle, compatibility requirements, and example usage without describing a product-specific add-on.
plannedUpstreamChanges.publicContractImpact: Documents the proposed public contract; adds no runtime behavior.
plannedUpstreamChanges.attributionMarkerStrategy: No source marker: documentation attribution is carried by Git history and this manifest.

localOnlyChanges.purpose: Track the Sidebar Steroids feature requirements, decisions, provenance policy, and verification scope.
localOnlyChanges.publicContractImpact: None. This tracker is not an upstream API change.

localOnlyChanges.purpose: Retain the source product concept for STATUS, GIT, and FILES as design context rather than implementation evidence.
localOnlyChanges.publicContractImpact: None. This product vision is not an upstream API change.

localOnlyChanges.purpose: Define the Sidebar Steroids product requirements, installability contract, architecture boundary, acceptance criteria, and delivery gates.
localOnlyChanges.publicContractImpact: None. The PRD is not an upstream API change; it specifies the separately distributed add-on and the generic host capability it requires.

localOnlyChanges.purpose: Define the human-readable contribution, provenance, marker, refresh, CI, and release-gate protocol.
localOnlyChanges.publicContractImpact: None. This protocol is not an upstream API change; it documents a possible contribution without implementing one.

localOnlyChanges.purpose: Record machine-readable upstream provenance, planned file scope, local-only scope, verification requirements, and release gates.
localOnlyChanges.publicContractImpact: None. The manifest is not an upstream API change; it records plans and evidence without implementing an API change.

changeAccounting.refreshProcedure: Before opening a contribution candidate, diff the candidate head against the pinned base, record every changed path and zero-context hunk in the matching plannedUpstreamChanges entry, classify each path, and update this accounting block. Do not infer attribution from commit messages alone.
changeAccounting.ciCompletenessPolicy: For an implementation candidate, fail CI when any changed upstream file is absent from plannedUpstreamChanges, when a path is classified both upstream and local-only, or when an implemented upstream entry has no refreshed file and hunk evidence.

For an implementation candidate, exit status 0 confirms that every changed upstream file is represented in the manifest; a non-zero status lists missing paths. This checker is a planned CI artifact and is not created by the documentation-only task.

requiredChecks.expectedEvidence: Review shows truthful compatibility wording, a distinct primary add-on name, and no claim of official status, sponsorship, endorsement, or permission to use upstream marks.

requiredChecks.command: test -f LICENSE && node -e 'const p=require("./package.json"); if (!p.license || !p.name || !p.repository) process.exit(1)'
requiredChecks.expectedEvidence: For the separately distributed add-on, exit status 0 confirms that it has an explicit license, identity, and repository metadata. The add-on must carry any upstream MIT notices required for copied upstream code.

releaseGates.evidence: The upstream LICENSE is retained, the MIT notice remains in copies or substantial portions, and any required third-party notices are present.
User-facing text uses truthful compatibility wording, does not imply official status or endorsement, uses a distinct primary name, and has no confusingly similar upstream package or project name.
Git author metadata, an accurate Co-authored-by trailer where appropriate, the manifest, and the PR identify andrikonbeat without rewriting upstream history.
The add-on has its own explicit license and package metadata, is not labeled as a modified gentle-pi distribution, and includes the upstream MIT notice for any copied upstream code.
Actual changed files and zero-context hunks against the pinned base are classified and recorded before submission; no planned entry is presented as implemented without diff evidence.
CI fails when a changed upstream file is missing from the manifest or is classified as both upstream and local-only.
The upstream PR contains only the generic host seam, its tests, and generic documentation; Sidebar Steroids product behavior, branding, and package delivery remain outside that PR.
Focused contract, layout, cleanup, and default-Status regression tests pass, and the add-on fails closed when the host API is absent or incompatible.
